newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDANSK SHIPYARD WINS FINANCING FOR ONE SHIP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDANSK SHIPYARD WINS FINANCING FOR ONE SHIP.

text.p: The owner of Poland's nationwide television Polsat agreed to finance the construction by the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard of one of three ships commissioned by a German shipowner, PAP news agency said on Thursday.
Last week Gdansk yard's receiver agreed to build for Scholler Holdings Ltd three ships, each worth $27.5 million.
But PAP quoted Polsat as saying that its owner Zygmunt Solorz would offer financing of the two remaining vessels only after he received from Gdansk's suppliers guarantees of timely deliveries.
The contract renewed hopes that the historic shipyard, where the Solidarity movement that helped topple communism was born 17 years ago, could be revived.

Under the contract, the first ship is to be ready on April 20 next year and the last on September 30, 1998. The contract will allow the rehiring of up to 2,500 workers by the yard, which has had to dismiss all but 370 employees out of its 7,000-strong workforce since June, 1996, when the company filed for bankruptcy with debts of 415 million zlotys.
The government is seeking an investor to buy the yard, whose book value amounts to $88 million.
According to the BMF consulting firm responsible for collecting offers 21 bids have been placed so far.
